items.title: Smart Window: Finish what you start online

items.title: Bookmark search on iPad isn't competitive with Chrome
items.content_text: Currently Firefox on iPadOS does not have a dedicated search dialog for bookmarks. When you open the bookmark dialog on iPad, you can navigate bookmark folders, but you can't search. Supposedly you can enter a bookmark keyword in the address bar, but Firefox on iPad doesn't show a match in the result drop down list, even if bookmark search is enabled in settings. Note that on iPad, unlike the desktop, you can't prefix an asterisk to bookmark keywords to indicate you are doing a bookmark search.

items.title: Needs more customisation
items.content_text: ​I've been using Firefox Nightly as my main browser, and it's genuinely awesome. Huge praise for the privacy features, overall convenience for regular users, great speed, and extension support. ​However, compared to the desktop version, the mobile customization is still quite limited. One specific feature that's missing and really needs to be added is the ability to set a custom background image on the home screen. Please consider adding this option! Keep up the great work.

items.title: Why is IMAP Email Server Not Responding? How Can I Fix It?
items.content_text: The IMAP Email Server Not Responding issue occurs when an email client cannot properly communicate with the IMAP server. Common causes include incorrect IMAP credentials, unstable internet, disabled IMAP, outdated email clients, server downtime, firewall or antivirus restrictions, full mailbox storage, and outdated passwords. The guide recommends checking server settings, using an app password when required, verifying internet connectivity, checking service status, freeing mailbox space, and upd

items.title: Feature Request: Require Fingerprint Authentication Before Autofilling Saved Passwords
items.content_text: Firefox should provide an option to require Windows Hello authentication, such as fingerprint verification, whenever a saved account is selected for autofill. The desired flow is: Login page → Click Firefox's suggested account → Windows Hello appears → Fingerprint verification → Authentication successful → Firefox fills the username and password. This would provide an additional layer of security and prevent saved credentials from being autofilled without user authentication.

Enabling the next iteration of the borrow checker on nightly
items.content_text:
TL;DR We are enabling the next iteration of the borrow checker (coined Polonius Alpha)
on nightly in preparation for stabilization in the next few months.

Whaaaaaat?
Yes! You heard it right! The next iteration of the Rust borrow checker is coming! Rust's first borrow checker ("AST borrowck") was very limited and was phased out in 2019 in favor of NLL, other than a "migrate mode" that was used to provide nice error messages. items.title: Launching Interop 2025
items.content_text: Interop 2025 continues the mission to make the web more consistent across browsers, building on 2024’s 95% interoperability score. This year, 19 focus areas target key developer needs and long-standing issues, including WebRTC improvements, Storage Access API, and CSS Zoom. items.title: Is Memory64 actually worth using?
items.content_text: After many long years, the Memory64 proposal for WebAssembly has finally been released in both Firefox 134 and Chrome 133. In short, this proposal adds 64-bit pointers to WebAssembly.

items.content_text: Mozilla and Filament have introduced Uniffi for React Native, a tool that allows developers to leverage the safety and performance benefits of Rust in cross-platform React Native apps. You’re free to explore more than a half-million community created themes on addons.mozilla.org (AMO), or better yet, create your own custom theme. Best of all — create a theme featuring a beloved pet! Then you can take your little buddy with you wherever you go on the web. items.title: Llamafile v0.8.14: a new UI, performance gains, and more
items.content_text: Discover the latest release of Llamafile 0.8.14, an open-source AI tool by Mozilla Builders. With a new command-line chat interface, enhanced performance, and support for powerful models, Llamafile makes it easy to run large language models (LLMs) on your own hardware. Learn more about the updates and how to get involved with this cutting-edge project. items.title: 0Din: A GenAI Bug Bounty Program – Securing Tomorrow’s AI Together
items.content_text: As AI continues to evolve, so do the threats against it. As these GenAI systems become more sophisticated and widely adopted, ensuring their security and ethical use becomes paramount. 0Din is a groundbreaking GenAI bug bounty program dedicated specifically to help secure GenAI systems and beyond. In this blog, you'll learn about 0Din, how it works, and how you can participate and make a difference in securing our AI future. items.title: Announcing Official Puppeteer Support for Firefox
items.content_text: We’re pleased to announce that, as of version 23, the Puppeteer browser automation library now has first-class support for Firefox. This means that it’s now easy to write automation and perform end-to-end testing using Puppeteer, and run against both Chrome and Firefox. The post Announcing Official Puppeteer Support for Firefox appeared first on Mozilla Hacks - the Web developer blog .

items.title: Snapshots for IPC Fuzzing
items.content_text: Process separation remains one of the most important parts of the Firefox security model and securing our IPC (Inter-Process Communication) interfaces is crucial to keep privileges in the different processes separated. We take a more detailed look at our newest tool for finding vulnerabilities in these interfaces – snapshot fuzzing. The post Snapshots for IPC Fuzzing appeared first on Mozilla Hacks - the Web developer blog .

items.title: Sponsoring sqlite-vec to enable more powerful Local AI applications
items.content_text: Today we’re proud to announce the next Mozilla Builders project: sqlite-vec. Led by independent developer Alex Garcia, this project brings vector search functionality to the beloved SQLite embedded database. Alex has been working on this problem for a while, and we think his latest approach will have a great impact by providing application developers with a powerful new tool for building Local AI applications. items.title: Experimenting with local alt text generation in Firefox Nightly
items.content_text: Firefox 130 will introduce an experimental new capability to automatically generate alt-text for images using a fully private on-device AI model. The feature will be available as part of Firefox’s built-in PDF editor, and our end goal is to make it available in general browsing for users with screen readers. items.content_text: When Mozilla’s Innovation group first launched the llamafile project late last year, we were thrilled by the immediate positive response from open source AI developers.
